_knightComment: The control plane this shop takes its optional Features from. Off until a credential is issued: adding the agent must not change how the shop starts. Set Knight__ClientId and Knight__ClientSecret in the environment and never in this file, and point FeatureRoot at a volume that survives a restart - a container that mounts nothing there loses every installed Feature on every deploy.

Wallet._comment: ManualTopUpEnabled is off: card-to-card means a person reading a bank statement and deciding whether an image is genuine, and turning it on commits the store to staffing that queue. The flow is built and tested either way. Amounts are Toman.

_serilogComment: Serilog reads its own section, not Logging:LogLevel — so the overrides that keep production logs readable have to be here. EF Core logs every command it executes at Information, which on this shop came to 736 SELECT statements in ten minutes: a log nobody can search, a disk that fills, and the database's schema written out on every page view. Warning keeps the failures and drops the narration. Development turns the commands back on, where reading them is the point.
_comment: No ConnectionStrings:Bojan, Jwt:SigningKey or TrustedProxy:ApiKey here on purpose — production has no default that works, matching the frontend's AUTH_SECRET and ADMIN_DEV_PASSWORD. Set ConnectionStrings__Bojan, Jwt__SigningKey and TrustedProxy__ApiKey as environment variables or in a secret store. Seed:Enabled stays false so a production database is never filled with the design's demo catalogue by accident.
